Random.name: Random
Random.description:
🎲 Fortune favors the bold: begin wherever chance decrees.

📍 A busy public place: a station, a mall, a beach, Tokyo, Hosu or Yokohama's harbor.
📅 Sunday, March 31: the day before U.A.'s year begins.
👥 For every Path.
Random.storyStart:
Generate a story start tailored to the player's chosen traits. Draw on world lore to build a vivid situation in a concrete place, alive with everyday noise, spring light, and street smells. The opening should present clear immediate circumstances while leaving many paths open. Weave in the character's background without forcing a predetermined plot. The story opens on Sunday, March 31, the day before U.A.'s new academic year begins; a U.A. student or teacher is out for the day and due back on campus by evening.

BUILDING THE OPENING (this start has no fixed scene):
- Open inside the place the engine chose, on a sight, sound, or smell happening right now, with you already there for the reason your Path hook and Background give.
- Give the opening one small, concrete pressure that belongs to a bustling public spot: a spilled bag, a dropped wallet, a delayed train chime, a laughing crowd around a street performer, a lost stranger asking the way, an eager fan pushing for a photo, a minor Quirk mishap.
- Give you a first choice you can answer in one action, plus a thread worth revisiting later: a stranger's name, a favor owed, a striking face in the crowd.
OPENING HOOKS (one per Path; use the one that matches, otherwise the Default):
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A) or (Class 1-B): signed out on the dorm sheet for a final errand before classes; the sign-out ends at curfew, and a late return reaches your homeroom teacher by morning.
- U.A. General Studies: a last afternoon out with family or old friends from home; someone asks, a little too gently, why you did not try for the Hero Course.
- U.A. Support Course: hunting parts, tools, or materials for a first build; a curious shop clerk asks what all the heavy gear is for.
- U.A. Management Course: watching how a crowd reacts to flashy hero ads and merchandise, notes open on your phone.
- U.A. Faculty: a quiet day off before first lessons, an unfinished lesson plan, and a working pro's sharp habit of spotting trouble.
- Licensed Sidekick: walking an agency patrol with a crackling radio, or off duty and bound by the same Quirk laws as everyone else.
- Licensed Pro Hero: recognized by an excited voice in the crowd while your agency phone keeps buzzing in your pocket.
- League of Villains Recruit: here to meet a broker's go-between carrying directions, cash, or a burner phone, somewhere in this crowd and not yet spotted.
- Independent Villain: working, scouting, or collecting in the press of bodies, tracking every street camera.
- Vigilante: out of costume and off your usual streets, watching a brewing problem the police will not reach in time.
- Civilian Life: a work shift, an errand, or a Sunday outing, with a Quirk that rarely matters on the clock.
- Default: you are waiting for someone who is running late when small trouble breaks out nearby.
UPBRINGING TOUCHES (add one if it fits the PC):
- Mutant: a passerby stares a beat too long at your heteromorph features, or quietly shifts to make room without a word.
- Hero Family: a relative's smiling face beams from a poster or bright screen nearby, and someone in the crowd makes the connection.
- Police Family: you know by heart how long a patrol response takes here and what a formal statement involves.
- Criminal Ties: a face in the moving crowd belongs to your family's old circle, and their eyes just locked onto yours.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Canon people appear only where their records place them at the chosen location, as themselves on their own business, two at most in the first turn.
- A wanted villain whose record places them nearby stays completely out of sight in the opening.
- U.A.'s canon students and faculty are back on campus today; a U.A. character out in town meets only strangers.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Step in by hand and voice: catch a heavy door, scoop up what fell, step squarely between two tense people, ask what happened.
- Call for help: the uniformed staff in charge of the venue, the police on 110, or a pro's agency if you know one.
- Watch, follow, or film on a phone, and offer a witness statement later.
- Walk on and keep to your own Sunday; the trouble resolves or grows on its own causes.
- Use your Quirk, and carry whatever the law and the watching crowd make of it.
PUBLIC PLACES:
- Every busy place has people in charge who arrive first: station staff and a local koban police box, uniformed mall guards with radios, attendants, shop owners. Pros arrive only when called, after real time passes, unless one is already patrolling nearby.
- Crowds film anything with a Quirk in it. Phones come out fast, a clip can hit the evening news, and a registered Quirk caught on camera leads police straight to a name.
- A pro in costume draws a noisy crowd, photo requests, and street complaints in equal measure; out of costume, only die-hard fans know a face.
- Japan runs on small, crisp courtesies: IC cards beeping at ticket gates, warm rice balls and canned coffee at any convenience store, prices in yen, neat queues kept, apologies offered first.
CONSEQUENCES BY PATH:
- A U.A. student who uses a Quirk off campus gives a police statement like anyone else, and their homeroom teacher hears of it.
- A sidekick or pro on duty files a report and claims the case; off duty, they answer to the law for what they did.
- A villain or vigilante seen using a Quirk becomes a fresh description in a police file and a viral clip on someone's phone.
- A civilian who steps in gets earnest thanks, a tedious statement, and sometimes a stern lecture.
THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on its first moment):
- U.A. students and faculty head back to campus by evening, and tomorrow morning brings the first day of classes.
- Sidekicks and pros return to agency calls, villains to brokers and debts, vigilantes to dark streets nobody patrols, civilians to work, rent, and family.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the exact place and area the engine chose; any travel is the player's choice.
- Your Quirk works exactly as your traits state; public use outside self-defense or licensed duty is illegal for everyone, U.A. students included.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; you know only what your Path and Background allow.
- If several player characters start here together, each has their own Path reason to be present; their shared history is only what their Backgrounds state.
- End on an open, living moment the player can answer, without writing your choice.
Random.questGenerationGuidance: Quests grow from the place the opening chose and the PC's Path, then move to the Path's home ground: U.A. students and faculty to campus and the first week of classes, sidekicks and pros to their agency's calls, villains to brokers and debts, vigilantes to the streets nobody patrols, civilians to work, rent and family. A thread from the opening (a stranger met, a favor owed, a thief seen) may return later as a small personal quest. Keep the first quests local and small; for a U.A. character, the sign-out, curfew and first day of classes set what they can take on today.
